tags.name: App
tags.description: App configuration and the home screen.

endpoints.description: Branding, detected features and app rules set in the plugin settings. Called on every app start.
Sections in the order chosen in the plugin settings. Signed-out users get the public sections only.

endpoints.summary: Get the owner's translations of the app's own texts in one language
endpoints.description: Served by the Yallapp platform for every app, also those on WordPress or their own API: the app takes the address from `Config.languages.list[].strings.url` and never builds it. The pack has the owner's translations of the app's interface strings (the keys of the app's string files); the app shows the owner's string, else its own in that language, else English. Keep the last pack for offline use and download it again when `strings.version` in `/config` changes. Strings with placeholders use the same ICU format as the app's string files (`{name}`, `{count, plural, =1{…} other{…}}`), checked when the owner saves them. With `draft=1` and `X-Yallapp-Preview`, the app preview gets the Pages & look draft's strings.

tags.name: Pages
tags.description: Pages and bottom tabs built in the client dashboard.

endpoints.summary: Get the bottom tabs and the list of pages
endpoints.description:
The navigation and pages the client published in the dashboard. When nothing is published yet, the server sends default pages and tabs for the app type, built from the site's content, so the answer is always a full navigation. Servers without pages (older plugins) return 404; the app then uses its built-in tabs and `/home`.

The default pages follow `app_type`, the type of the app asking, so they match its screens from the first start. Without it the server uses the type the owner chose in the dashboard, else a guess from the site's plugins. Published pages don't depend on it.

Send `If-None-Match` with the last `version` to get 304 when nothing changed.

endpoints.summary: Get one page with its blocks
endpoints.description: Blocks in the order set in the dashboard, with lists (courses, products, services, posts, listings) already resolved. Blocks meant only for signed-in or signed-out users are filtered here. On iOS, blocks and items never carry purchase actions for paid content. 99.3 So are blocks the owner shows only between two dates, on the other platform or in other languages (than the one asked for with `Accept-Language`): the app never gets them.

endpoints.summary: Send the answers to a form block by email
endpoints.description: Roadmap 99.4. For a `form` block whose `send_to` is `email`: the server checks the answers against the published block (each field it knows, required fields filled, an email or phone that looks like one, a choice among its options, at most 2,000 characters each) and emails them to the business: the hosted API to the app's support email (else its owner's), the plugin to the support email it has from Yallapp (else the site's admin email). With a signed-in person's token, their name and email go with the answers. A form whose `send_to` is `chat` is sent by the app as a chat message instead (`POST /chat/conversations/{conversation_id}/messages`), which needs the person signed in. At most 5 answers a minute and 30 a day from one address, counting only answers that pass the checks.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Sign-in with a one-time code, tokens and sign-up.

endpoints.description:
Sends a 6-digit code to the phone number. Rate limited per number and per IP.

On a WordPress site the plugin's settings choose who sends it: Yallapp (the default: the plugin makes the code and Yallapp delivers it on WhatsApp) or Digits (through the gateway set up in Digits; needs Digits' REST API add-on). Either way the account is the one with that number on the site, so people who signed up with Digits keep their accounts. The hosted API sends codes itself.

Demo apps on the hosted API (the apps on yallapp.com.tr/demo) send no code: only the public demo number signs in, with the fixed code shown on that page. Any other number is refused with 403 `demo_number_only`. The demo number is limited per IP and per app, and works in demo apps only.

The app preview in the Yallapp dashboard sends `preview: true`, and only when `Config.auth.preview_sign_in` is true. Such a request never sends a code: only the store review number signs in, with its fixed code. Any other number is refused with 403 `preview_review_number_only`.

On the hosted API the store review number (and address) skips the per-number and per-IP limits, as reviewers sign in again and again, but is limited per app: 30 requests an hour for the number and the address together, then 429, so its fixed code can't be guessed. The plugin applies its usual limits to them.

endpoints.summary: Send a sign-in code by email
endpoints.description:
Sends a 6-digit code to the email address, when `Config.auth.methods` has `email` and `Config.auth.email_sign_in` is `code` (the hosted API, and WordPress sites whose owner chose email codes). Same rules as phone codes: valid for 5 minutes, 5 attempts, a new code after a minute, limited per address and per IP. Verify it with `POST /auth/otp/verify`; an address with no account gets a `signup_token` (when sign-up from the app is allowed), and `POST /auth/register` then asks the same details as a phone sign-up (the email is already known).

The email comes from the app's own email address when its owner set up their own email server in the Yallapp dashboard, else from Yallapp's address with the app's name. On WordPress the plugin makes the code and Yallapp delivers it; an account that can edit the site never signs in by code (it gets no email and the code is refused), so staff sign in on the website.

Refused with 403 `method_not_allowed` when the app doesn't offer email sign-in. Demo apps sign in only by phone: 403 `demo_number_only`.

Store review: the app's store review email address (for apps that sign in by email only, where reviewers can't use the review number) gets no email and signs in with the fixed review code. The app preview (`preview: true`) never sends a code: only the store review address signs in there, and any other address is refused with 403 `preview_review_number_only`.

endpoints.summary: Sign in with email and password
endpoints.description:
For servers whose `Config.auth.email_sign_in` is `password` (a WordPress site: its own accounts and passwords, checked by WordPress with the site's own rules and security plugins). Only existing accounts sign in here; people without an account sign up by phone or on the website (or, where the owner chose email codes, with `POST /auth/email/request`). A wrong address and a wrong password get the same 400 `invalid_credentials`, so the answer never tells whether an account exists. Limited per address and per IP. Devices and the device limit work as for phone sign-in.

Refused with 403 `method_not_allowed` when the app doesn't offer email sign-in. In the app preview only the store review email address signs in; anything else gets 403 `preview_review_number_only`.

Store review on WordPress: with the plugin's store review access on, its test email address signs in with the fixed code as the password, to the site's account with that address (made when there is none and sign-up is allowed; never an account that can edit the site).

Verifies a code from `POST /auth/otp/request` or `POST /auth/email/request`. Returns tokens for an existing account. For a phone number (or email address) with no account, returns a one-time `signup_token` to use with `POST /auth/register` (only when sign-up from the app is allowed).

A new phone number is refused with 403 `app_user_limit` when the app has as many users as its plan allows (apps on the hosted API only; a WordPress site keeps its users and has no limit). The error carries `contact`, so the app can show how to reach the app's owner. People who already have an account keep signing in.

Fields required here follow the "Required at sign-up" plugin setting. Refused with 403 `app_user_limit` (with `contact`) when the app reached its plan's number of app users since the code was verified.
Exchanges a refresh token for new tokens. The old refresh token stops working (rotation). Roadmap 68: also while the app is paused, so a signed-in person can still delete their account.
Also while the app is paused (roadmap 68).

tags.name: Yallapp sign-in
tags.description:
For a client's own API whose owner chose "Yallapp signs people in" on the dashboard's App sign-in page (roadmap 34). Yallapp's hosted API for the app (`https://yallapp.com.tr/api/app/{app_id}`, `Config.auth.base_url`) serves `GET /config` (only its `auth` counts), the Auth endpoints (`/auth/otp/request`, `/auth/email/request`, `/auth/otp/verify`, `/auth/register`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`), `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /me`, `GET /me/devices` and `DELETE /me/devices/{device_id}`, with the sign-in methods, codes, store review access and device limit the owner set in Yallapp. The client's API serves everything else, including `/auth/checkout-link`, `PUT /me/push-token` and the notifications, and never the sign-in endpoints.

The access token the app sends to the client's API is a JWT signed with ES256 (header `kid`) by a key pair of that app only, valid for 15 minutes. Claims: `iss` (`https://yallapp.com.tr`), `aud` (the app's ID), `sub` (the person's Yallapp user ID, a string), `phone` (E.164) and `email` only when proven by a code, `name`, `iat`, `exp`; `did` is Yallapp's own. The client's API checks the signature with the keys at `GET /.well-known/jwks.json`, and `iss`, `aud` and `exp`, then finds or creates its own user by `sub`, or by the proven phone or email. A missing, expired or invalid token answers 401, and the app refreshes it at Yallapp. Refresh tokens are opaque and work once; signing out, removing a device and deleting the account end them. Before deleting the account at Yallapp, the app calls the client's `DELETE /me`, so the client can delete its own data (404 or 405 when it keeps none). Roadmap 49: whatever that call answers (an error, no answer), the app then deletes the account at Yallapp, and Yallapp sends the client's API a signed notice, the `accountDeleted` webhook (`POST <API address>/webhooks/yallapp`), retried until the API answers 2xx. The client deletes the person by `sub` from either, whichever comes first.

endpoints.summary: Get the keys that sign access tokens
endpoints.description: Served only by Yallapp's hosted API, for an app on its own API that Yallapp signs people in to (404 otherwise): the app's public ES256 keys as a JSON Web Key Set, the one signing now first. When the owner replaces the key, the old one stays here for a day, so tokens it signed keep working until they expire. Cache it for up to 5 minutes (`Cache-Control`), and fetch it again when a token names a `kid` you don't have.

endpoints.summary: A person deleted their account (sent to the client's API)
endpoints.description:
Roadmap 49. Sent by Yallapp to an app on its own API that Yallapp signs people in to, at `<API address>/webhooks/yallapp`, when a person deletes their account in the app. Yallapp has deleted the account already; the client deletes what it keeps about `sub`.

The body is a Security Event Token (RFC 8417): a JWT signed with the app's ES256 key, the one that signs its access tokens, checked with the same key set (`GET /.well-known/jwks.json`). Its header has `typ` `secevent+jwt`; its `aud` is `<app ID>:events`, never the access tokens' audience, so a notice never passes as an access token. Each try is signed again (`exp` 5 minutes after `iat`); `jti` stays the same on every try and is also in `Yallapp-Delivery`.

Answer 2xx once it's received; repeats of a `jti` should answer 2xx too. A 5xx, 408, 425 or 429 answer, no answer within 10 seconds (5 for the first try) or an API that can't be reached is tried again after 1, 5 and 30 minutes, 2, 6, 12 and 24 hours (8 tries); any other answer stops it (404 or 405: the API doesn't take notices). Redirects aren't followed, and an address on a private network isn't called. The notices of the last 30 days and how each went are on App sign-in › For your developer, where a failed one can be sent again: it starts over with the same `jti` and the same tries.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The signed-in student's profile, devices and push token.

endpoints.description: In a demo app everyone shares one account, which can't be changed (403 `feature_disabled`).

Required by Apple and Google. Deletes or anonymises the WordPress user according to the site's policy and signs out every device. In a demo app (one shared account) it signs out this device only.

Roadmap 68: it keeps working while the app is paused (its plan ended, or the owner's account is suspended), together with `POST /auth/refresh` and `POST /auth/logout`, on WordPress (plugin 0.4.6) and on the hosted API. The app offers it on its paused screen to someone who is signed in.
In a demo app, only the current device, and `limit` 0 (no limit).

endpoints.summary: Register this device for push notifications
Say how many items the cart holds
endpoints.description: Roadmap 85.3: the app keeps the cart on the phone and says how many items it holds whenever that changes (0 once it's empty or ordered), so a shop on Yallapp's hosted API can send "You left something in your cart" once, 3 hours after the last change, when the owner hasn't turned it off. Nothing else about the cart is sent. Servers that don't need it answer 404, and the app doesn't ask again until it restarts.

tags.name: Catalog
tags.description: Categories, courses and course details.

endpoints.description: Published courses. A private course (WordPress's Private visibility, which the LMS uses to hide a course from its catalog) is never listed, not even to its students: they find it in `GET /me/courses` (50).

A private course opens only for the students enrolled in it (bought, free or added by an administrator) and for whoever may read it on the website (its author, editors and administrators); anyone else gets `404 not_found`, as for a course that doesn't exist (50). A course with a password on the website (roadmap 62) shows in the catalog and opens as `password_protected`; see `CourseDetail`.

endpoints.summary: Get a course's topics and items
endpoints.description: The course's topics (Tutor LMS topics, LearnPress, LearnDash and MasterStudy sections, LifterLMS sections, Sensei modules...) in the order the LMS shows them, each with its lessons, quizzes, assignments and live classes in order. Items the student can't open are returned with `locked` set and no content. A private course's curriculum is `404 not_found` for whoever can't open the course (`GET /courses/{course_id}`, 50). A course with a password on the website (62) has no topics for a student who isn't in it.

tags.name: Learning
tags.description: Enrolled courses, lessons and progress.

endpoints.description: Roadmap 73. Clears the signed-in student's progress in the course (lessons completed, where each video stopped, and the quiz results the LMS keeps with the course, where it does) so they can take it again from the first lesson. Their enrollment, orders, reviews and questions stay. The app offers it ("Start the course again", after asking to confirm) on a finished course whose `CourseDetail.can_restart` is true, then opens the first lesson. `403 not_enrolled` for a student who isn't in the course, `403 restart_disabled` when `can_restart` is false (the owner turned it off for the course, or the LMS has no way to reset a student's progress). A certificate already issued is the LMS's: some keep it, some take it back.
Private courses the student is enrolled in are listed too (50).

Empty when the LMS has no wishlist (`features.wishlist` is false). Roadmap 62: a private course the student may open (enrolled in it, or may read it on the website) is listed like any other; one they can't open isn't.

endpoints.summary: Add a course to the wishlist
endpoints.description: Fails with `feature_disabled` when the LMS has no wishlist (`features.wishlist` is false). A course the student can't open (a private one they aren't in) is `404 not_found` (62).

endpoints.summary: Remove a course from the wishlist
endpoints.description: Fails with `feature_disabled` when the LMS has no wishlist (`features.wishlist` is false).

Free-preview lessons are public; everything else requires enrollment. A lesson of a private course is `404 not_found`, free previews included, for whoever can't open the course (`GET /courses/{course_id}`, 50); so is a lesson of a course with a password on the website for a student who isn't in it (62).
Fails with `watch_requirement_not_met` when the site requires a share of the video to be watched first.

endpoints.summary: Links to save a lesson for offline viewing
endpoints.description: Roadmap 45. When `features.downloads` is true and the lesson's `offline.available` is true, the app asks for the lesson's files here and keeps them on the phone, encrypted, in its own storage. Each link is for this student only and works for a short time (`expires_at`): the app downloads at once, and asks again to resume a download after that. A lesson whose video plays from a video site (YouTube, Vimeo, Bunny Stream and other players) can't be saved: 409 `not_downloadable`, with `details.reason` as in `LessonOffline`. 403 `feature_disabled` when downloads are off for the app, 403 `not_enrolled` when the student can't open the lesson.

endpoints.summary: Whether the student may keep their saved lessons
endpoints.description: Roadmap 45. The app sends the lessons it keeps for offline viewing when it starts with a connection. A lesson is `refused` when the student can't open it any more (their enrollment ended, was refunded or expired, or the lesson is gone); the app deletes it. The app also deletes everything when `downloads` is false (the owner turned downloads off or the plan no longer includes offline mode), and a lesson it hasn't been able to check for `keep_days` days.

endpoints.summary: List the student's memberships and subscriptions on the website
endpoints.description: Roadmap 90.3. When `features.memberships` is true: the student's current Paid Memberships Pro levels, WooCommerce Subscriptions (active, on hold or cancelled but running until the end of the paid period) and LearnDash groups. Managed on the website: the app shows them and never sells them (no purchase buttons on iOS).
Empty when the LMS has no certificate feature active.

tags.name: Quizzes
tags.description: Quiz questions, attempts and results.

endpoints.summary: Get quiz details and the student's attempts

endpoints.description: Returns the questions. Questions of a type the app can't show natively are returned with `render_mode` `webview` and a signed `webview_url`.

tags.name: Commerce
tags.description: Free enrollment, checkout hand-off and the student's orders.

endpoints.summary: Get a one-time signed-in checkout link
endpoints.description: Android only, and only when the "Enroll now on Android" setting is on. The link signs the student in on the website and opens the checkout for the course. It works once and expires after 5 minutes.

91.4 Loyalty points of shops without a website (`StoreConfig.loyalty`): the balance, what it is worth, and the latest changes, newest first. Points are earned when an order is completed (what was paid for the products, after coupons and points), used in the cart (`CartInput.use_points`), given back when a paid order that used them is cancelled or refunded, and taken back when an order that earned them is refunded or its return approved. `feature_disabled` (403) when the shop has no loyalty points.

Orders from the site's checkout (the LMS's own or WooCommerce, or the hosted API's payment page for shops without a website), newest first. Empty when the site doesn't sell (`features.orders`). The Academy app on iOS doesn't show orders, as it doesn't sell courses; Store apps show them on both platforms. 96.3 Apps without a website that sell tickets (Events), paid courses (Academy) or memberships (gyms' Bookings) list those orders here too, each with its `receipt_url`, and the app shows them under My orders (Events and gyms on both platforms).

endpoints.summary: Get one of the customer's orders
endpoints.description: One order of the signed-in customer, for following it: a restaurant's order shows `fulfilment` and `fulfilment_status`, which change as the kitchen works on it (received, preparing, ready, out for delivery, completed). Each change also reaches the customer as a notification, whose push `data` carries the `order_id`. 91.2 Shop orders too: a shipment with its tracking, completed, cancelled or refunded is an `order_update` notification (unless the phone turned `orders` off) that opens this; on Yallapp's hosted API, shops on Shopify and the other connected platforms too (their orders are looked at for 30 days after a checkout from the app, every 15 minutes). `not_found` for someone else's order.

91.3 The customer asks the shop to take back an order it completed, within `StoreConfig.returns.days` (`Order.can_return`). The shop approves or declines it (with a reply) on its side; the customer is told with an `order_update` notification. Once asked, it can't be asked again (`conflict`); `forbidden` when the shop takes no returns from the app or the order can't be returned (not completed, too late, nothing physical).

A course with a password on the website (62) is `403 enrollment_disabled`: the student joins it on the website, where its password is entered. A course that needs a membership the student doesn't have (90.3, `CourseDetail.membership`) is `403 membership_required`.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: The notifications inbox.

endpoints.description: Every notification the site sent to the student, newest first, whether or not push reached a device: to everyone, to the students of a course they're enrolled in, or to them alone. Kept for 90 days.

tags.name: Store billing
tags.description: Roadmap 100. Courses and memberships bought in the app through Google Play Billing (Android) and the App Store's In-App Purchase (iOS), on Yallapp's hosted API for every app (`Config.store_billing.base_url`), as the stores ask for digital content. The app buys with the store's own SDK, then sends what the store gave it to `POST /billing/purchases`; Yallapp checks it with Google or Apple, records it once and gives the access where the course lives (the hosted API, the WordPress site through the plugin's `POST /billing/access`, Teachable or Thinkific through their enrolment APIs, or an app's own API through the `purchase.completed` notice). Refunds and ended subscriptions take it back. Roadmap 100.7: for an app on its own API, and for Teachable or Thinkific courses the platform's API doesn't price, the owner lists what the app sells on Dashboard › In-app purchases (each course's ID, title and price; each membership plan's ID, title, price, period and the course IDs it opens). Physical goods and services (shop products, orders, appointments, tickets to a venue, gym memberships, donations) keep their payment pages.

endpoints.summary: A store billing token for the signed-in person (WordPress)
endpoints.description: Roadmap 100. Served by the Yallapp plugin (0.4.23 and later) when `Config.store_billing.session` is `site`, like `POST /chat/session`: the plugin gets the token from Yallapp (`POST /billing/sessions` in the platform API) for the signed-in person's WordPress user ID, display name and email. The app sends it as `Authorization: Bearer` to `Config.store_billing.base_url` until `expires_at` (one hour), and asks again on 401 `invalid_token`.

endpoints.summary: What the app sells through the store on this platform
endpoints.description: Roadmap 100. Served by the hosted API at `Config.store_billing.base_url` for every app that sells in the app. The store product IDs of the paid courses and membership plans the owner sells, ready in the store. The app asks the store for each product's price in the person's currency and shows that price, never the site's. Public: no token needed.

endpoints.summary: Send a purchase the store made, for the access it buys
endpoints.description:
Roadmap 100. After the store's purchase flow says the purchase went through (Android: `purchased`; iOS: a verified transaction), the app sends the Google purchase token or the App Store's signed transaction. Yallapp checks it with the store (that it is this app's, for this product, paid and not refunded), records it once, gives the access (enrolment in the course, or the membership until `expires_at`) and acknowledges it with the store. Only then does the app finish the transaction with the store. Sending the same purchase again answers the same grant. A purchase the store marks pending (`status` `pending`, Android) gives nothing yet: Yallapp gives the access when Google tells it the purchase completed.

`invalid_receipt` (400): not a valid purchase of this app's product. `purchase_in_use` (409): the purchase gives access to another account of this app already (a store account buys for one app account). `store_unavailable` (503): the store couldn't be reached; the app keeps the transaction unfinished and sends it again later (at the next start too). A purchase never acknowledged is refunded by Google after three days.

Roadmap 100. "Restore purchases" (which Apple asks for): the app sends every purchase the store has for the person (Android: the purchase tokens of `queryPurchases`; iOS: the signed transactions of `Transaction.currentEntitlements`), and gets back the grants still active for this account. Purchases already in use by another account of the app are left out, never moved.

endpoints.summary: A purchase in the store gives or takes access (sent to the client's API)
endpoints.description:
Roadmap 100. Sent to an app on its own API that Yallapp signs people in to and that sells in the app, at the same address and signed the same way as `account.deleted` (a Security Event Token with the app's key), once Yallapp has checked a store purchase (`purchase.completed`), and when Google or Apple says it was refunded, revoked or ended (`purchase.revoked`) or renewed (`purchase.completed` again, with a later `expires_at`). The client gives or takes the access in its own system. Retries and `Yallapp-Delivery` are as for `account.deleted`; the delivery log, with "Send again", is on Dashboard › In-app purchases.

Roadmap 100.7. `jti` (and `Yallapp-Delivery`) is the same for every try of one change of one purchase, and a new one for its next change (a renewal, a refund): give or take the access once per `jti`, and answer 2xx to repeats. Answer 2xx only once the access is given or taken: until a `purchase.completed` is delivered, the app hears `store_unavailable` and Yallapp doesn't acknowledge the purchase with Google (which refunds a purchase not acknowledged within three days). A notice still waiting for another try when the purchase changes again is dropped, never sent late: the newer notice says how things stand.

tags.name: Chat
tags.description: Roadmap 77. A person and the business (`direct`), and course groups in academies (`group`), on Yallapp's hosted API (`Config.chat.base_url`). People never talk to each other in private. Text, photos, videos, voice messages and files; files count in the app's storage and show in the business's Media library. Messages are kept a year, and longer when the business chooses; the business moderates (reports, blocking, deleting) and is responsible for what is said in its chat. Deleting one's account (`DELETE /me`, on the hosted API or a WordPress site) deletes the person's messages and files too.

endpoints.summary: A chat token for the signed-in person (WordPress)
endpoints.description:
Roadmap 77. Served by the Yallapp plugin only (0.4.9 and later): the chat lives on Yallapp, and a WordPress app's people sign in on the website, so the app asks its site for a chat token, which the plugin gets from Yallapp (`POST /chat/sessions` in the platform API) for the signed-in person: their WordPress user ID, display name and picture, and for an academy the courses they're enrolled in (their groups). The app then calls `Config.chat.base_url` with this token until `expires_at` (one hour), and asks again on 401 `invalid_token`.

The hosted API and Yallapp sign-in don't need it: the app uses its own access token on `Config.chat.base_url` (`Config.chat.session` is `access_token` there).

Served by the hosted API (`Config.chat.base_url`) for every app with chat. The conversation with the business (`kind: direct`) always comes first, made on the first call; then, in an academy that turned on course groups, the group of each course the person is enrolled in, most recent message first. Students never talk to each other in private: there are only these two kinds.
A cheap call for the badge, made when the app opens and comes back to the front.

Newest first with `before` (older pages), or oldest first with `after` (what arrived since the last message the app has). While the conversation is on screen the app asks with `after` every `poll_after_seconds` (3 while messages come, up to 15 when it's quiet); a push brings it back when the app isn't open. Messages a person blocked (`ChatMember.blocked`) are left out for them; a deleted message stays in place as `deleted: true` without its text or file.

Text (up to 4,000 characters), a finished upload (`upload_id`, from `POST /chat/uploads`), or both. `client_id` makes it safe to send again after a network error: the same `client_id` in the same conversation answers the message already made. Members the business blocked can read but not send (403 `chat_blocked`). 60 messages a minute per person.

endpoints.summary: Mark a conversation read up to a message

endpoints.description: Names and pictures only, never a phone number or an email address. The business's team shows as the business.
Deleted for everyone, with its file. Others see that a message was deleted.

endpoints.summary: Report a message to the business
endpoints.description: The business sees the report in its dashboard and Yallapp Business and decides (delete the message, block the sender). Once per person and message; a second report answers 204 too.
For the person asking only, in every group. The business itself can't be blocked.

endpoints.summary: Start sending a photo, video, voice message or file
endpoints.description: Checks the type and size (pictures 20 MB, videos 200 MB, voice messages 20 MB, files 50 MB: PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, text) and the app's storage, where chat files count with the Media library's (413 `storage_full`). The app sends the file in chunks to `upload_url` exactly as Yallapp Business does for Media (the media gate's protocol), then calls `/complete`, then sends the message with `upload_id`. An upload not sent in a message within a day is deleted.

endpoints.summary: A fresh link to carry on with an upload

endpoints.description: 409 `incomplete` with the offset reached when part of the file is missing.

tags.name: Community
tags.description: Course reviews and questions and answers. On Yallapp's hosted API (roadmap 63) the business answers questions and may reply to a review (`Review.reply`) or hide it from others (`hidden`, shown to its author only). Roadmap 64: the business may also hide a question or a single answer (`CourseQuestion.hidden`, `QuestionAnswer.hidden`); a hidden one reaches its author only, never other students' lists or counts.

endpoints.description: Approved reviews, newest first, with the rating summary. Signed-in students also get their own review, approved or not.

endpoints.summary: Write or edit the student's review
endpoints.description: One review per student and course. Enrolled students only. The site may hold it for approval (`status`). On Yallapp's hosted API (roadmap 63) a student writes or edits at most 20 reviews an hour in an app (429).

Questions students asked in the course, newest first, without their answers. Enrolled students only. A question the business hid (roadmap 64) is listed only for its author, with `hidden`, and isn't in `total` for others.

endpoints.summary: Get a question with its answers
endpoints.description: A question the business hid (roadmap 64) is `404` to everyone but its author. Hidden answers are listed only for their author.

tags.name: Store
tags.description: WooCommerce products, the cart and the checkout hand-off, for Store apps. The cart lives in the app; the order is placed on the site's own checkout, opened with a one-time link that fills the WooCommerce cart.

endpoints.summary: Get the store home screen sections
endpoints.description: Sections in the order chosen in the plugin settings. Only sections with content are returned.
Categories with products, in the site's own order. `parent_id` builds the tree.
Published products the shop shows (catalog visibility "shop" or "shop and search"; "search" when `search` is given).
Approved reviews, newest first, with the rating summary. Fails with `feature_disabled` when the site has reviews turned off.
Checks the app's cart against the shop: current prices, stock and quantity limits. Nothing is saved. Shipping, taxes and coupons are added on the site's checkout.

endpoints.summary: Get a one-time checkout link for the cart
endpoints.description:
On WordPress, the link fills the site's WooCommerce cart with these lines, keeps the delivery date and gift message for the order, signs the customer in when they are signed in to the app, and opens the checkout; it works once. On the hosted API it opens the shop's checkout (Shopify's or another connected platform's, or our payment page for shops without a website). The link expires at `expires_at`. Signed-out customers get a link only when the shop allows guest checkout (`store.guest_checkout`). The checkout's last page has `order-received` or `thank_you` in its address, so the app knows the order was placed.

A `coupon` (91.1) goes with the order: applied on the site's checkout (WooCommerce, or a connected platform's discount link) or on our payment page; one that doesn't apply any more is left out, never an error.

With `use_points` (91.4, shops without a website), the signed-in customer's loyalty points take their value off the order on our payment page: as many as they have then, up to what the products cost after the coupon. They are used when the order is paid.

Fails with `cart_changed` (409) when a line is no longer available, with `one_product_at_a_time` (409) when the shop's checkout can only take one product from the app (show the message), and with `purchase_not_allowed` (403) for digital products on iOS.

Shops with `store.fulfilment` (restaurants and cafés) also take how the order is collected: `fulfilment` (`pickup` or `delivery`, one the shop offers), a `delivery_address` for delivery, and `scheduled_for` (one of the `slots` of `GET /store/order-times`; null or missing for "as soon as possible"). They fail with `kitchen_closed` (409) for an order as soon as possible while closed (show the message; a scheduled time may still work), `below_minimum` (409) when a delivery's subtotal is under `store.fulfilment.min_order`, `outside_delivery_area` (400) when the district isn't one of `store.fulfilment.delivery_areas`, and `invalid_request` (400) for a missing address or a time that isn't offered. The delivery fee is added to the order on our payment page. Prices, options and fees are always computed by the server.

endpoints.summary: When the kitchen takes orders now
endpoints.description: For shops with `store.fulfilment` (restaurants and cafés): whether they're open now, when they open or close next, whether an order "as soon as possible" can be placed now, and the times a scheduled order can be for. Computed in the shop's time zone at the time of the request, so the app asks again before checkout. `not_found` for shops without `store.fulfilment`.

endpoints.summary: List the user's conversations with the office
Get a conversation with its messages
endpoints.description: Marks the office's messages as read.
Writing again reopens a conversation the office closed. Refused with 403 while the office has messages turned off.

tags.name: News
tags.description: Articles and categories, for News & blog apps (roadmap 23). Read-only and free to read: there is no paid content. WordPress serves the site's published posts (never private or password-protected ones); the hosted API serves articles written in the Yallapp dashboard or read from the site's RSS or Atom feed. An article's body is processed like lesson content (`render_mode`, `html` with embed placeholders, `embeds`).

endpoints.description: Featured articles (sticky posts on WordPress, featured in the dashboard; the newest on a feed), the latest articles (without repeating those) and a rail per category with articles, newest first. Empty lists are sent as empty arrays; rails without articles are left out.
Categories with published articles, in the site's own order.
Published articles, newest first (or in the order of `ids`).
A published article with its body, processed like a lesson's content.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Events and tickets, for Events & tickets apps (roadmap 28): events with their days and times, a venue or an online link, and ticket types. Free tickets are taken in the app; paid tickets are bought on the web payment page and issued only once the payment is confirmed. Each ticket has a random code and a signed QR payload, checked once at the door. Tickets to events at a venue are physical-world services, bought on Android and iOS; tickets to online-only events (no venue) are digital content, so iOS never offers buying them (free tickets work everywhere). Served by the hosted API.

endpoints.summary: Get the filters the events list offers
endpoints.description: The categories of upcoming published events, with how many each has, and the days of the first and last upcoming event, for the list's filters and the calendar.

Published events, soonest first. Without `from`, events that haven't ended yet; a cancelled event stays in the list with `status: cancelled` until it would have ended. `from` and `to` are days in `EventsConfig.time_zone`, both included.

A published event with its description (processed like a lesson's content), pictures, venue, ticket types and what each ticket type's button does on this platform (`TicketType.action`). The online link is sent only to people holding a ticket. Signed-in users get `my_tickets`.

Free ticket types only, on every platform. One ticket per name in `attendee_names` (the signed-in user's name for the rest), at most the ticket type's `max_per_order`. Places are taken atomically: fails with `sold_out` (409) when there aren't that many left, with `sales_ended` (409) after the ticket type's sales end or once the event started, with `event_cancelled` (409), and with `purchase_required` (403) for a paid ticket type.

endpoints.summary: Get a one-time link to buy paid tickets
endpoints.description: Holds the places and opens the web payment page; the tickets are issued only once the payment is confirmed, and show in `GET /me/tickets` then. Places that aren't paid for are freed after the link expires. Fails with `purchase_not_allowed` (403) on iOS for online-only events (no venue: digital content) and when the organiser can't take card payments, and with `sold_out`, `sales_ended` or `event_cancelled` (409) like `register`. The payment page's last page has `order-received` in its address.
Every ticket issued to the signed-in user, upcoming events first (soonest first), then past ones. The app keeps the last answer on the device, so tickets and their QR codes show without a connection.

endpoints.summary: Cancel one of the user's tickets
endpoints.description: Free tickets only, when the organiser allows it (`EventsConfig.allow_cancel_hours`) and the event starts at least that many hours later; the place goes back on sale. Fails with `cancel_not_allowed` (403) otherwise, and with a conflict (409) for a ticket already used or cancelled. Paid tickets are refunded by the organiser.

tags.name: Donations
tags.description: Campaigns and donations, for Charity & donations apps (roadmap 29). Campaigns are managed in the Yallapp dashboard and served by the hosted API. The donation itself is paid on a web page, into the charity's own payment account: in the iPhone app always in the system browser (App Store guideline 3.2.2), on Android in the app or in the browser as `open_in` says. A donation counts towards a campaign only after the payment is confirmed.

endpoints.description: Open campaigns first (featured ones first, then the newest), then campaigns that have ended. Drafts are never listed.
An open or closed campaign with its story, processed like an article's body, and its most recent donations (anonymous ones without a name).

endpoints.summary: Get a one-time link to the donation page
endpoints.description:
Starts a donation and returns the page where the donor pays. The donor's name and email for the receipt are asked on that page.

`open_in` is always `browser` when `platform` is `ios`: an iPhone app may not take donations itself (App Store guideline 3.2.2), so the app opens the link in the system browser, never in a web view inside the app, and words the button "Donate on our website". On Android it is `in_app` (Google Play's billing rules don't cover donations to charities; the app may still open it in the browser).

Fails with `invalid_request` (400) for an amount under the campaign's `min_amount`, a custom amount the campaign doesn't allow, or `recurring: monthly` when `DonationsConfig.monthly` is false; with `campaign_closed` (409) when the campaign has ended; with `purchase_not_allowed` (403) on iOS when `DonationsConfig.ios_mode` is `off`; and with `donations_unavailable` (503) while the charity's payments aren't set up.
Confirmed donations started from the app while signed in, newest first, each with its receipt; 47 refunded ones too, with `refunded_total`.

tags.name: Delivery
tags.description: Roadmap 104. Delivery and courier companies, on Yallapp's hosted API. The customer sends a parcel: picks a service, the pickup and drop-off places, sees the price before sending, and pays cash to the courier or by card on the company's payment page (its own iyzico, Kashier, Fawaterk, Stripe or PayPal account), as the company allows (`DeliveryConfig.payment`). Delivery is a service in the physical world, so the card payment page opens in the app on Android and iOS alike. Prices follow the company's choice (`DeliveryConfig.pricing`): by distance (a straight line between the two places, so both need their coordinates), by the drop-off zone, or one fixed price; a service may add its own amount. The customer follows the shipment by its stages, or also sees the courier on a map while it is on the way when the company chose live tracking (`DeliveryConfig.tracking`).

endpoints.description: The services a customer can choose (same-day, express, documents...), in the company's order. Empty when the company has none; the shipment then has no service.

endpoints.summary: Price a shipment before sending it
endpoints.description: The price of sending a parcel between two places with a service. Fails with `invalid_request` (400) when a place needs its coordinates (pricing by distance), the zone is missing or unknown (pricing by zone), or the places are further apart than the company delivers (`DeliveryConfig.max_distance_km`).

endpoints.summary: Read a place's coordinates from a maps link
endpoints.description: For a place shared as a Google Maps or Apple Maps link (a WhatsApp location, a short `maps.app.goo.gl` link): the coordinates it points at. Only links of those maps are followed. Fails with `invalid_request` (400) when the link has no coordinates.

Creates the shipment at the price `POST /delivery/quote` gives for the same places and service. Paid in cash (`payment: cash`), it waits for a courier at once (`pending`). Paid by card (`payment: card`), it waits for the payment (`awaiting_payment`) and the answer has `pay_url`, the company's payment page, opened in the app on both platforms (a service in the physical world); it waits for a courier once the payment is confirmed.

Fails with `invalid_request` (400) as the quote does, or for a payment method the company doesn't take (`DeliveryConfig.payment`); with `payments_unavailable` (503) for a card payment while the company's payments aren't set up.
Newest first; `active` only those not yet delivered, failed or cancelled.

The shipment with its stages, its courier and, with live tracking while the courier has it (`picked_up`, `on_the_way`), where the courier is. The app asks again every 15 seconds or so while the screen is open and the shipment is active.
Only before a courier has it (`awaiting_payment`, `pending`). A shipment paid by card is refunded by the company. Fails with `not_cancellable` (409) once a courier has it.

endpoints.summary: Get a new payment link for a shipment
endpoints.description: For a shipment still `awaiting_payment`, when the first link was closed or ran out. Fails with `not_payable` (409) for any other.

tags.name: Courier
tags.description:
Roadmap 104. The courier's screens. A courier is a person the company added on the dashboard's Couriers page by mobile number (or by email, for apps that sign in by email only); whoever signs in to the app with that number, proven by its code, is that courier (`User.roles` has `courier`). Every endpoint here answers `not_courier` (403) to anyone else, and to couriers the company paused. Couriers see only the jobs given to them, and, when the company lets couriers take jobs (`DeliveryConfig.assignment` is `open`), the jobs waiting for a courier, without the customer's and recipient's numbers until they take one. The courier's position is sent while the app is open and they have a job on the way, kept only while it is, and shown only to the customer of that job.

Where these screens are depends on the company's choice (`DeliveryConfig.courier_app`): `same`, in the company's app, shown only to couriers, who can switch between their courier screens and the customer's; `bundle`, in the company's second app made for couriers (build config `delivery_role: courier`), while its customer app has none; `yallapp_courier`, in the shared Yallapp Courier app, while the company's app has none.

endpoints.description: Only couriers on duty are offered new jobs and told of them.

`active`: the courier's jobs not yet delivered, oldest first. `available`: shipments waiting for a courier, oldest first, only when the company lets couriers take jobs and the courier is on duty (else empty). `done`: the courier's delivered, failed and cancelled jobs of the last 30 days, newest first.
One of the courier's jobs, or one waiting for a courier that they could take.
Only when the company lets couriers take jobs and the courier is on duty. The first courier to take it gets it; the others get `job_taken` (409).

endpoints.summary: Move a job to its next stage
endpoints.description: In order: `picked_up` (the parcel is with the courier), `on_the_way`, then `delivered`, or `failed` when it couldn't be delivered (with a `note`). A cash shipment is paid once delivered: the courier collected `CourierJob.collect`. `released` gives a job that isn't picked up back to the company (to other couriers when they take jobs themselves). Fails with `invalid_status` (409) for any other step.

Sent every 20 seconds or so while the app is open and the courier has a job picked up or on the way (no position is taken in the background). Kept only while they have one; answered 204 and dropped otherwise. At most one every 5 seconds is kept.

tags.name: Food
tags.description: Roadmap 105.1. Food delivery from many restaurants, on Yallapp's hosted API. The company adds its restaurants with their menus; the customer picks a restaurant (`GET /food/restaurants`), fills one restaurant's cart, sees the total before ordering (`POST /food/quote`: the dishes, their choices, the delivery fee by the company's delivery prices from the restaurant to the customer, and the restaurant's smallest order), and orders, paying cash to the courier or by card on the company's payment page as the company allows (`FoodConfig.payment`). The restaurant accepts the order with the time it needs, or turns it down; the company's couriers deliver it (the Courier tag: each order's delivery is a courier job, picked up at the restaurant). The customer follows the order's stages, and the courier on a map while it is on the way when the company chose live tracking, then rates the restaurant and the courier.

endpoints.description: The company's active restaurants: open ones first, then by `sort`. With the customer's position (`lat`, `lng`) each has its distance and whether it delivers there (`delivers`); restaurants that don't are listed last. `cuisine` keeps one cuisine (`FoodConfig.cuisines`), `q` searches restaurant and dish names.
The restaurant and its menu in sections, the company's order. Sold-out dishes are listed with `available` false.

The cart's lines with their prices, the subtotal, the delivery fee to the drop-off and the total. Fails with `invalid_request` (400) for a dish or choice the restaurant doesn't have (or a missing required choice), with `unavailable_item` (409) for a sold-out dish (`field` names the line), `restaurant_closed` (409) while the restaurant is closed or busy, `below_minimum` (409) under the restaurant's smallest order, and `outside_delivery_area` (400) when the restaurant doesn't deliver to the drop-off.

Places the order at the prices `POST /food/quote` gives for the same cart. Paid in cash, it goes to the restaurant at once (`placed`). Paid by card, it waits for the payment (`awaiting_payment`) and the answer has `pay_url`, the company's payment page, opened in the app on both platforms (food delivered is a service in the physical world); it goes to the restaurant once the payment is confirmed. Fails as the quote does, for a payment method the company doesn't take, and with `payments_unavailable` (503) for a card payment while the company's payments aren't set up.

endpoints.summary: List the signed-in customer's food orders
endpoints.description: Newest first; `active` only those not yet delivered, turned down or cancelled.

The order with its stages, the courier and, with live tracking while the courier has it (`picked_up`, `on_the_way`), where the courier is. The app asks again every 15 seconds or so while the screen is open and the order is active.
Only before the restaurant accepts it (`awaiting_payment` or `placed`); then `not_cancellable` (409). A card payment already made is refunded by the company.

endpoints.summary: A new payment page for an order waiting for its payment

endpoints.description: Once, after it is delivered, within 7 days. The restaurant's rating counts in its average; the courier's is seen by the company.

tags.name: Restaurant
tags.description: Roadmap 105.1. A restaurant's screens. Its staff are people the company added to the restaurant on the dashboard by mobile number (or by email, for apps that sign in by email only); whoever signs in with that number, proven by its code, works for that restaurant (`User.roles` has `restaurant`). Every endpoint here answers `not_restaurant` (403) to anyone else, and to staff of a restaurant the company paused. Staff see their restaurant's orders only: new ones (with a push and a sound), accept each with the minutes it needs or turn it down with a reason, mark it ready for the courier, and set the restaurant busy for a while (no new orders) or open again.

endpoints.summary: The restaurant the signed-in person works for
Busy for a while, or open again
endpoints.description: `busy_minutes` 15 to 240 stops new orders for that long; 0 opens again. Opening hours still apply.

`new`: waiting to be accepted, oldest first; `active`: accepted and not yet picked up, the soonest ready first; `done`: picked up, delivered, turned down or cancelled in the last 2 days, newest first.

endpoints.summary: Accept a new order with the minutes it needs
endpoints.description: From `placed` only; then `invalid_status` (409). The customer is told when it will be ready, and, when the company makes courier jobs on acceptance (`FoodConfig.courier_job`), a courier job is made at once.
From `placed` only. The customer is told the reason; a card payment is refunded by the company.

endpoints.summary: The order is ready for the courier
endpoints.description: From `accepted` only. Makes the courier job when the company makes them once orders are ready (`FoodConfig.courier_job`).

tags.name: Rides
tags.description: Roadmap 105.2. Ride hailing, on Yallapp's hosted API. The rider sets the pickup and the drop-off, sees each of the company's vehicle types with its fare (`POST /rides/estimate`) and asks for a ride now or, when the company allows it, at a later time (`POST /rides`). The company's drivers get the request one at a time, nearest first, each with a few seconds to accept (`RidesConfig.matching`), or the company gives it to a driver from the dashboard. The rider follows the driver to the pickup and along the ride on the map, can share the ride with a link, call the company's emergency number, cancel (with the company's fee once the free minutes after a driver accepted are over), pay the fare in cash to the driver or by card on the company's payment page, and rate the driver. Fares, fees and the company's share are the company's: Yallapp sets none of them.

endpoints.summary: The fare of each vehicle type between two places
endpoints.description: Both places need their coordinates. The distance and time are estimated from the straight line between them (the road is taken as a third longer, at the company's usual speed), so the fare is `upfront` (the one the rider pays, plus waiting) or an estimate when the company charges what the meter says (`RidesConfig.fare_mode`). Vehicle types without an online driver nearby are listed with `available` false (asking for one still waits for a driver). Fails with `outside_service_area` (400) when the pickup is outside the company's areas, with `invalid_request` (400) for a place without coordinates or an unknown promo code (`field` names it), and with `rides_unavailable` (503) while the company has no vehicle type with fares.

At the fare `POST /rides/estimate` gives for the same places, vehicle type and promo code. Now: it is offered to the drivers at once (`searching`). Later (`scheduled_at`, when `RidesConfig.scheduling` allows it, 30 minutes to 7 days ahead): it waits (`scheduled`) and is offered 15 minutes before. A card ride is paid once it ends, on the company's payment page (`POST /me/rides/{ride_id}/pay`). An unpaid cancellation fee from the rider's last ride is added to this one's fare.

Fails as the estimate does; with `ride_in_progress` (409) while the rider has another ride that isn't over (scheduled ones aside); with `invalid_request` (400) for a payment method the company doesn't take or a time it doesn't allow; with `payments_unavailable` (503) for a card ride while the company's payments aren't set up.
Newest first; `active` only those not yet completed or cancelled (scheduled ones too).

The ride with its stages, its driver and car and, from the driver's accepting until the ride ends, where the driver is. The app asks again every 5 seconds or so while the screen is open and the ride is active.

Before it starts (`scheduled`, `searching`, `accepted`, `arrived`); then `not_cancellable` (409). Free while no driver has it, and for `RidesConfig.cancellation.free_minutes` after a driver accepted; after that the company's fee (`cancellation.fee`) is charged, added to the rider's next ride.

For a card ride `completed` and not paid yet, the company's payment page (good for 60 minutes), opened in the app on both platforms (a service in the physical world). Fails with `not_payable` (409) for any other.
Once, after the ride is completed, within 7 days; then `already_rated` or `not_ratable` (409). The rating counts in the driver's average; the comment is seen by the company.

tags.name: Driver
tags.description:
Roadmap 105.2. The driver's screens. A driver is a person the company added on the dashboard's Drivers page by mobile number (or by email, for apps that sign in by email only), with their car; whoever signs in with that number, proven by its code, is that driver (`User.roles` has `driver`). Every endpoint here answers `not_driver` (403) to anyone else, and to drivers the company suspended. A driver goes online to get ride requests; while online, the app sends the driver's position (only while it is open), which is used to offer rides nearest first and shown to the rider of their ride; it is dropped when they go offline. The rider's number is shown once the driver accepted, until the ride ends.

Where these screens are depends on the company's choice (`RidesConfig.driver_app`): `same`, in the company's app, shown only to drivers; `bundle`, in the company's second app made for drivers (build config `role: driver`), while its riders' app has none.

endpoints.description: Only online drivers are offered rides. Going offline drops their position; it is refused with `ride_in_progress` (409) while they have a ride that isn't over.

Sent every 5 to 10 seconds while the app is open and the driver is online (no position is taken in the background). Kept only while they are online; answered 204 and dropped otherwise. At most one every 3 seconds is kept. During a ride, the positions also measure the distance the meter charges (`RidesConfig.fare_mode` `metered`).

endpoints.summary: The ride offered to the driver now
endpoints.description: A ride offered to this driver, with when the offer ends (`offer_expires_at`); at most one at a time; empty when none is or the driver is offline. The app asks every 3 seconds or so while online and free, and on a `ride_offer` push. The rider's number is not shown until the driver accepts.
`active`: the driver's ride that isn't over (at most one). `done`: their completed and cancelled rides of the last 30 days, newest first.
One of the driver's rides, or the one offered to them now.
While it is offered to this driver; then `offer_expired` (409). The rider is told the driver is on the way.

endpoints.summary: Let the ride go to the next driver
endpoints.description: The offer ends at once and isn't made to this driver again. Answered 204 also when it had already ended.

endpoints.summary: Move a ride to its next stage
endpoints.description: In order: `arrived` at the pickup, `in_progress` once the rider is in (with the rider's `pin` when `RidesConfig.pin` is true; a wrong one is `wrong_pin`, 400), then `completed` at the drop-off, which works out the final fare (shown on the answer's `fare`); a cash ride is paid once completed: the driver collected `collect`. `cancelled` before the ride starts, with a `reason`: `rider_no_show` (only `RidesConfig.cancellation.no_show_minutes` after arriving; the rider is charged the cancellation fee) or `other` (the ride goes back to the next driver). Fails with `invalid_status` (409) for any other step.
The driver's completed rides over today, this week (from Monday) or this month, in `RidesConfig.timezone`, with each day's totals.

tags.name: Bookings
tags.description: Services, staff, free times and appointments, for Bookings apps. The plugin reads them from the site's booking plugin (Amelia, BookingPress or LatePoint); the booking plugin's own rules decide the free times and whether a new appointment is approved or waits for the business. Appointments are paid at the business.

endpoints.summary: Get the bookings home screen sections
endpoints.description: Sections in the order chosen in the plugin settings. Only sections with content are returned.
Categories with services customers can book, in the booking plugin's order.
Services customers can book online, in the booking plugin's order.

endpoints.summary: Get a service and the staff who provide it

endpoints.description: Free start times from `from` for `days` days, by the business's local date, as the booking plugin computes them (working hours, days off, breaks, existing appointments, buffers and how far ahead customers may book). Without `staff`, a time is free when any staff member who provides the service is free; `staff_ids` says who.

Books a free time for the signed-in customer, through the booking plugin, so its emails, calendar sync and approval rules apply. The appointment is `approved` or `pending` as the plugin decides.

Fails with `slot_taken` (409) when the time is no longer free and with `invalid_request` (400) for a service, staff member or time that can't be booked.

When `bookings.intake_fields` lists questions (a clinic's intake form), `answers` holds the customer's answers by field ID. Fails with `invalid_answers` (400) when a required answer is missing or an answer doesn't fit its field; `details.fields` then maps field IDs to messages safe to show. Answers are health data: only the customer (in their appointments) and the business (in its dashboard) see them, and no push, email or text message includes them.
Upcoming ones soonest first, past ones (and cancelled ones) newest first.

endpoints.summary: Get one of the customer's appointments
Cancel one of the customer's appointments
endpoints.description: Fails with `too_late` (409) when it starts sooner than `bookings.cancel_before_minutes` allows, or when the business doesn't let customers cancel.

tags.name: Classes
tags.description: Group classes and memberships, for gyms, studios and coaches (Bookings apps; the hosted API only for now). Classes come from the business's weekly timetable; each has a capacity, and a spot is booked only while one is left. When `bookings.classes.membership_required` is true, booking needs an active membership, and a plan with credits uses one per class (given back when the customer cancels in time). Memberships are paid on a web page outside the app, on Android and iOS alike: they are for a service used in person (App Store Review Guideline 3.1.3(e)).

endpoints.description: Classes from `from` to `to` (both included, the business's local dates), soonest first, also full and cancelled ones. Signed-in customers get `booked` for their own spots. Answers `not_found` (404) when the app has no classes.

endpoints.summary: Book a spot in a class
endpoints.description: Books one spot for the signed-in customer, only while one is left (no overbooking, also when many book at once). Booking a class already booked answers it again. Fails with `class_full` (409), `too_late` (409) once it has started or is closer than `min_minutes_ahead`, `class_cancelled` (409), `membership_required` (403) without an active membership when the business asks for one, `membership_frozen` (403, roadmap 64) when the active memberships are frozen on the class's day, and `no_credits` (403) when the membership's credits are used up. With a credit plan, one credit is used.

endpoints.summary: Cancel the customer's spot in a class
endpoints.description: Gives the spot back. A credit used for it comes back too. Fails with `too_late` (409) when the class starts sooner than `bookings.classes.cancel_before_minutes` allows, or when customers can't cancel in the app, and with `not_found` (404) when the customer has no spot in it.

endpoints.summary: List the membership plans on sale
endpoints.description: Plans in the business's order. Empty when it sells none in the app.

endpoints.summary: Get a payment page link for a membership
endpoints.description: Opens the business's payment page for one plan; paying starts the membership at once. The page's last address has `order-received` in it. Offered on Android and iOS: a membership is for a service used in person, not digital content. Fails with `feature_disabled` (403) when the business can't take card payments, and with `not_found` (404) for a plan not on sale.
Active ones first (the one that ends first), then ended ones, newest first.

tags.name: Platform
tags.description: Calls from the Yallapp platform to a client's WordPress site (roadmap 31), never from the app. Only the Yallapp plugin serves them; the hosted API and a client's own API don't.

endpoints.summary: Push a new chat message to the site's app users
endpoints.description:
Roadmap 77. Sent by the Yallapp platform to a WordPress site when a message arrives for its app's people: the site keeps their push tokens, so its plugin sends the push (Firebase or Huawei Push Kit), with the notification preferences the person chose. Nothing about the message is stored on the site.

Signed like `POST /license/refresh`: `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `yallapp-chat-notify:<timestamp>:<sha256 of the notification JSON, hex>` keyed with the license key in capitals; a wrong signature, a site without a license key or a timestamp more than 5 minutes away is 401 `invalid_signature`.

endpoints.summary: Send a campaign from the Yallapp dashboard to the app's users
endpoints.description:
Roadmap 85.4. Sent by the Yallapp platform to a WordPress site when the owner sends a campaign from Dashboard › App notifications › Campaigns (now, at the time chosen, or each week): the site keeps its people's push tokens, so the plugin adds the notification to everyone's inbox (with its picture and what it opens) and pushes it to the phones that allow announcements, in batches. When the last batch is sent, the plugin reports how many phones it reached and missed with `POST /campaigns/report` (docs/api/platform.yaml).

Signed like `POST /chat/notify`: `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `yallapp-campaign:<timestamp>:<sha256 of the campaign JSON, hex>` keyed with the license key in capitals; a wrong signature, a site without a license key or a timestamp more than 5 minutes away is 401 `invalid_signature`. The same `send_id` twice is sent once (200 with the first answer).

endpoints.summary: Give or take access bought through a store
endpoints.description:
Roadmap 100. Sent by the Yallapp platform to the WordPress site (plugin 0.4.23 and later) once it has checked a store purchase, and again when Google or Apple says it was refunded, revoked, renewed or ended. The plugin gives the access (`grant`): enrols the user in the course (the site's LMS), or gives the membership until `expires_at` (Paid Memberships Pro level, LearnDash group, or the site's WooCommerce Subscriptions product), and records a WooCommerce order marked paid by the store when WooCommerce is active; or takes it back (`revoke`). `grant_id` is the same on every try of one change: a repeat answers as the first time did.

The request is signed like `POST /license/refresh`: the headers `Yallapp-Timestamp` (Unix seconds) and `Yallapp-Signature`, the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `yallapp-billing-access:<timestamp>:<the raw body>`, keyed with the license key in capitals. A wrong signature, a site without a license key or a timestamp more than 5 minutes away is refused (`invalid_signature`, 401). Only sent to the https address of the site the license is active on; tried again after 1, 5 and 30 minutes and 2, 6 and 24 hours when the site doesn't answer 2xx.

Sent by the Yallapp platform, a few seconds after the app's owner saves something the plugin reads from its license status (the app type, how people sign in, the plan) or publishes the app's pages. The plugin then checks its license with the platform and fetches the published pages, as it does on its own twice a day and every 15 minutes. It trusts nothing in this request: it only learns that it should ask now.

The request is signed with the site's license key, which both sides know: `signature` is the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of `yallapp-license-refresh:<timestamp>` keyed with the license key in capitals (`YALL-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX`). The plugin refuses a wrong signature, a site without a license key and a timestamp more than 5 minutes away from its clock (`invalid_signature`, 401). It checks at most once every 30 seconds: a nudge within 30 seconds of the last one gets 429 and the plugin checks once when the 30 seconds are over, so the last change still arrives. Reachable during maintenance and while the app API is paused, so a renewed or reactivated plan reaches the site.

tags.name: Links
tags.description:
Links that open the app (roadmap 46): Android App Links and iOS Universal Links. A shared course, product, service, listing, article, event, campaign or page is a link `<base>/<kind>/<id>`. It opens that screen in the app when the app is installed, and the website otherwise.

- On Yallapp's link domain, for every app: `<base>` is `https://yallapp.com.tr/a/<app_id>`. Without the app, that address shows a page in the app's branding with its store links; for a WordPress app it sends the visitor on to the site's own link. - On a WordPress site with the Yallapp plugin: `<base>` is `<site>/a` (`Config.links.share_base_url`). Without the app, the plugin sends the visitor to the item's own page on the site (its permalink), or to the home page when the item has none or isn't public.

| Kind | Link | Opens in the app | `id` | |---|---|---|---| | `course` | `<base>/course/12` | the course (Academy) | a number | | `product` | `<base>/product/12` | the product (Store) | a number | | `service` | `<base>/service/12` | the service (Bookings) | a number | | `listing` | `<base>/listing/12` | the listing (Real estate) | a number | | `article` | `<base>/article/431` | the article (News & blog) | letters, digits, `-` and `_` | | `event` | `<base>/event/12` | the event (Events & tickets) | a number | | `campaign` | `<base>/campaign/12` | the campaign (Charity & donations) | a number | | `page` | `<base>/page/offers` | a page built in the dashboard | its slug |

The same table, with examples, is `docs/api/app-links.json`; the app, the platform and the plugin follow it. A link of a kind the app type doesn't have, or that doesn't match, opens the app's home.

The phone checks that the domain trusts the app with two files the domain serves at its root, as JSON (`application/json`), without a redirect: `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` (Android: the package name and the SHA-256 fingerprints of the Play App Signing key and the upload key) and `/.well-known/apple-app-site-association` (iOS: `<Team ID>.<bundle ID>` with the paths `/a/*`, or `/a/<app_id>/*` on Yallapp's domain). The plugin builds them from its license status (`LicenseStatus.app_links` in `docs/api/platform.yaml`). Push notifications and notifications in the inbox may carry a `link` in the same format.

**The site's own pages** (roadmap 48). On a WordPress site, the plugin also lists in `apple-app-site-association` the paths of the site's own pages for what the app shows: courses and lessons, products and product categories, posts, and the pages with a booking plugin's booking form, as the site's permalinks make them. It leaves out, before them, what must stay on the website: `wp-admin`, `wp-login.php`, the REST API, feeds, `xmlrpc.php`, `wp-content` and `wp-includes`, the cart, checkout, account and payment pages of WooCommerce and the course plugins, and addresses with `add-to-cart`, `wc-api`, `rest_route` or `preview` in their query. Android's App Links have no exclusions, and the app's intent filters are fixed when it's built: the plugin reports the permalink bases that start with a fixed folder (`/courses/`, `/product/`, `/product-category/`, `/blog/`) with its license check (`SiteInfo.link_paths`), and the next build lists them. Posts whose permalinks start at the root of the site (`/%postname%/`) open the app on iPhone only.

The app asks `GET /links/resolve` what a page of the site is. When the answer is an item it shows, it opens that screen; otherwise (`kind` null, an error, an older plugin) it opens the address in its own in-app browser, which never hands the address back to the app, so a link never loops. A site in a folder (`example.com/learn`) can't serve the two files at its domain's root: the plugin serves them at `<site>/.well-known/…` too, for the domain's own server to copy, and until it does only Yallapp's links open the app.

endpoints.summary: What a page of the site is in the app
endpoints.description: Roadmap 48. The app asks what an address on the site that opened it is: a course, a lesson, a product, a product category, a post, or a page with a booking form. `kind` is null when the address is something else (the home page, a page, the cart, an account page, another site): the app then opens it in its in-app browser. Only public, published items are named. Served by the Yallapp plugin; the hosted API answers 404 (its links are always `<base>/<kind>/<id>`), and so do plugins released before this endpoint: the app then opens the in-app browser too.

tags.name: Crash reports
tags.description: Crash reports (roadmap 46). Served by Yallapp for every app, at `https://yallapp.com.tr/api/app/{app_id}`, also when the app's content comes from WordPress or an own API: the app sends its crashes to Yallapp, never to the site. Off when `Config.app.crash_reports` is false.

endpoints.description:
The app sends what went wrong (an uncaught error in the app's code), at most 10 reports per call, each one at most once per app run, with the sessions it counted since it last sent. Reports that couldn't be sent are kept on the phone (at most 10) and sent on the next start.

A report carries no personal data: no names, phone numbers, emails, tokens, codes or addresses with query strings. The app removes them before sending, and Yallapp removes what still looks like one before it stores the report. Yallapp groups reports by `fingerprint` (the error's type and its first frames in the app's own code), counting them, the first and last time seen and the app versions.

Rate limited per app and per address (`rate_limited`, 429 with `retry_after_seconds`). Answers 204 also when crash reports are off for the app, so the app doesn't keep them.
